title: Green Roofs and Heavy Rain
transcript:
Today we are looking at what happens to rain after it lands on a roof. In a city, a great deal of the ground is covered with hard surfaces. A conventional roof also sends most of its rainwater straight into the drainage system. If water arrives from many buildings at once, the pipes may be unable to carry it away quickly enough. This is one reason why streets can flood even when the rain does not last very long.

A planted roof changes that process. Its surface is made up of several layers, including a waterproof layer that protects the building. Above that lies a mixture of light material in which the plants take root. This is known as the growing layer. It can hold some of the rainwater, while the water that it cannot hold leaves more gradually. So a useful question is not only how much water runs off, but also when it runs off.

To study that distinction, researchers worked with two buildings on the same campus. The roofs were similar in size and exposed to the same weather, but only one was planted. The team fitted flow meters to the outlets on both buildings. These recorded the amount of water leaving each roof at regular intervals during a series of storms. The team then plotted each storm separately instead of comparing monthly totals. That made it possible to see a delay of a few minutes that a monthly figure would hide.

The largest difference occurred when heavy rain followed several dry days. The growing layer had had time to lose moisture, so it could take in more water at the start of the next storm. When storms came close together, however, there was little spare capacity left. That explains why the planted roof did not produce the same benefit in every storm.

Finally, the study covered only one growing season. The researchers could compare individual storms, but they could not determine whether older plants would behave in the same way. They plan to keep the instruments in place for another two years. In the meantime, the findings are useful when comparing drainage designs, as long as engineers allow for the possibility of several wet days in a row.

questions.prompt: A conventional roof sends most rainwater into the ____.
questions.explanation: 开头说明普通屋顶会把雨水直接送入排水系统。

questions.prompt: A planted roof holds some water in its ____.
questions.explanation: 种植屋顶的生长层会储存一部分雨水。

questions.prompt: Water leaving the roofs will be measured using flow ____.
questions.explanation: 研究人员安装了流量计，测量从两个屋顶流出的水量。

questions.prompt: When was the difference between the roofs greatest?
options: When it had already rained for a long time.
When a storm came after several dry days.
When the plants had reached maturity.
questions.answer: When a storm came after several dry days.
questions.explanation: 连续几天干燥后遇到暴雨，两种屋顶的差异最明显。

questions.prompt: What does the speaker identify as a limitation of the study?
options: The two roofs differed greatly in size.
The meters were installed too late to record any storms.
It observed only one growing season.
questions.answer: It observed only one growing season.
questions.explanation: 研究只持续了一个生长季，无法判断植物成熟后是否会出现相同效果。
